(p-536)In the name of Allah, the Entirely Merciful, the Especially Merciful.

Surah ash-Shams (The Sun).

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿By the sun and its brightness﴾ ﴿and by the moon when it follows it﴾ ﴿and by the day when it displays it﴾ ﴿and by the night when it covers it﴾ ﴿and by the sky and He who built it﴾ ﴿and by the earth and He who spread it out﴾ ﴿and by a soul and He who proportioned it﴾ ﴿and inspired it [with the knowledge] of its wickedness and its righteousness﴾ ﴿He has certainly succeeded who purifies it﴾ ﴿and he has failed who buries it [in corruption]﴾.

In these ten verses, Allah swears seven oaths by seven cosmic signs: the sun, the moon, the night, the day, the sky, the earth, and the human soul. Each sworn-by thing comes with a state, and all of them point to one matter: the success of the one who purifies that soul and the failure of the one who corrupts it. With each sign the oath is given to draw attention to its great, observed and tangible effect, which indicates overwhelming power.

This is as follows. First: ﴿By the sun and its brightness﴾. The sun alone is a sign indicating the power of its Creator, because of the thermal energy within it, which exceeds every estimate, and because it continues over time without diminution. So it is itself a sign.

Then comes the description of its effect, which is "its brightness" (ḍuḥāhā), namely the spread of its light at the forenoon of the day. This alone is a sign, because it is a result of its motion, and its motion is one of the signs of Allah, as He said, may He be exalted: ﴿And a sign for them is the night; We remove from it the day, and thereupon they are in darkness. And the sun runs on to its stopping point. That is the decree of the Exalted in Might, the Knowing﴾ [Ya-Sin: 37–38]. It is also the sign with which Ibrahim, peace be upon him, argued against Nimrod, in His saying: ﴿Indeed, Allah brings the sun from the east, so bring it from the west.' Then the one who disbelieved was confounded﴾ [al-Baqarah: 258].

In this course there is overwhelming power and extremely precise exactness. "Its brightness" is a result of this course. Then "its brightness" is abundant blessings upon the whole universe, through its spread over the earth and the benefit taken from its light and rays.

They have said: if it came closer by one degree or rose higher by one degree, no one could benefit from it at all, because it would burn by coming closer, and the world would freeze because of its distance. That is the decree of the Exalted in Might, the Knowing.

(p-537) So the forenoon brightness alone is a sign, and it is its heat, as in His saying: ﴿And that you will not thirst therein nor be exposed to the sun's heat﴾ [Ta-Ha: 119], meaning by the heat of the sun. And He, exalted, swore by the forenoon alone in His saying: ﴿By the morning brightness, and by the night when it becomes still﴾ [ad-Duha: 1–2].

As for His saying: ﴿and by the moon when it follows it﴾, the moon alone is likewise a sign, and so is its following of the sun, and the order of its course with this precision. This order is such that it does not outrun the sun, nor does the sun overtake it: ﴿It is not for the sun to overtake the moon, nor does the night outpace the day; and each, in an orbit, is swimming﴾ [Ya-Sin: 40].

In His saying, may He be exalted, ﴿when it follows it﴾, meaning it follows the sun, there is an indication of the movement of both, and that the sun precedes it while the moon follows.

It has been said: it follows the sun at the beginning of the month, when it sets, and it appears from the place where the sun set.

Some of the people of the science of the heavens (Ahl al-Hay'ah, astronomers) have said: it follows it in the rank of size, meaning that it is the greatest, and after it the other (bodies) is great in size. There is an observation on this.

No one can deny the benefits of the moon for creation: it lightens the darkness of the night, and it has some effects on crops. Its most important property is the marking of months by dividing the year, knowing the acts of worship such as fasting, pilgrimage, and zakat, the waiting period of women, expiations by fasting, the falling due of debts, and the conditions of transactions, and everything connected to reckoning in worship or dealing.

The oath by the moon has come in al-Muddaththir, in His saying: ﴿No! By the moon, and by the night when it withdraws﴾ [al-Muddaththir: 32–33], and in His saying: ﴿and by the moon when it becomes full﴾ [al-Inshiqaq: 18], which indicates the greatness of its sign and the precision of its indication.

His saying: ﴿and by the day when it displays it﴾. "The day" is one of the effects of the sun's light.

As for "it displays it" (jallāhā), it has been said that the pronoun in it refers to the sun, as in the one before it. But Ibn Kathir chose that it refers to the earth, meaning that it uncovered it and made clear everything in it, so that seeking livelihood and striving would be made easy, as in His saying: ﴿He is the One who made the night for you that you may rest therein, and the day giving sight﴾ [Yunus: 67], and His saying: ﴿And He is the One who made the night for you as a garment, and sleep for rest, and made the day for rising﴾ [al-Furqan: 47].

(p-538) Allah, exalted, has sworn by the day when it becomes manifest (tajallā), meaning it appeared and became clear, without a pronoun referring to something else, in His saying: ﴿And by the night when it covers, and by the day when it becomes manifest﴾ [al-Layl: 1–2], meaning that in contrast to the night's covering, there is the manifestation of the day.

Allah has shown the greatness of the sign of the day and the greatness of the sign of the night, and that none can bring them except Allah, as in His saying: ﴿Say: "Have you considered, if Allah made the night perpetual for you until the Day of Resurrection, what deity other than Allah could bring you light? Then will you not hear?" Say: "Have you considered, if Allah made the day perpetual for you until the Day of Resurrection, what deity other than Allah could bring you a night in which you may rest? Then will you not see?"﴾ [al-Qasas: 71–72].

As for His saying: ﴿and by the night when it covers it﴾, they said: it covers the sun, so its light is screened off. The discussion of the night is like the discussion of the day, in terms of being a sign and an indication of His power.

The sufficient texts have preceded, and the oath by the night will come in His saying: ﴿and by the night when it covers﴾ [al-Layl: 1], meaning it covers the whole universe, as in His saying: ﴿and by the night and what it gathers﴾ [al-Inshiqaq: 17], meaning it collects and encompasses with its darkness.

The pronoun in "it covers it" (yaghshāhā) refers to the sun. On this basis it has been said that the oath in these four refers entirely to the sun in different states: in its brightness, then its manifestation, then the moon's following of it, then the covering of it by the night. Here there is a question: how does the night cover the sun, when the night, which is darkness, is a result of the sun's setting away from the side on which the night is?

It has been answered that the night covers the sun's light so that darkness forms, but the reality is otherwise: the sun is visible and its light spreads, but in the part of the earth opposite to the darkness that exists, just as the darkness occurs in the part opposite to the day, and so on.

On this basis Ibn Kathir said: the pronoun in "it covers it" and "it displays it" refers to the earth, although there is a difference in the referent of the pronoun. And Allah knows best.

His saying: ﴿and by the sky and He who built it﴾. It has been said: "mā" here means "alladhī" (the one who), and it was used in place of "man" (who), which is used for those of knowledge, because "mā" carries the sense of description: meaning "by the sky and the Mighty One who built it." Likewise what follows it in "by the earth and what spread it out and [by] a soul and [Him] who proportioned it," and "the Wise, the Knowing" ((p-539) "who proportioned it"). "Mā" is shared between the knower and others, as in His saying: ﴿nor are you worshippers of what I worship﴾ [al-Kafirun: 3], and similarly: ﴿marry what seems good to you of women﴾ [an-Nisa: 3].

The conditions of the sky in its building and raising, and in making it seven heavens, have been mentioned many times before. In those texts He explained how it was built, and that He, glorified and exalted, built it with strength, as in His saying: ﴿And the sky We built with might﴾ [adh-Dhariyat: 47], meaning with strength.

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿and by the earth and He who spread it out﴾ [ash-Shams: 6], like "spread it out" (daḥāhā) [an-Nazi'at: 30].

They have said: the substitution of "ṭā'" for "dāl" is well known, and ṭaḥā comes with the meaning of "created" and with the meaning of "went away" in every thing. From the first is the verse:

"Jadhimah does not know who created her, nor who dwells in the high throne."

From the second is the saying of ʿAlqamah:

"A heart has been swayed by you among the beauties, a heart longing, which restores youth when old age has come."

There is no contradiction in this: He, exalted, created it and extended it, and took its extremities in every direction, meaning in its extension.

**Notice.**

They said: The mention of the sky and "He who built it" is to indicate its having been created (ḥudūth), and consequently the creation of the sun and the moon, and that their governance belongs to God.

As for His saying: ﴿By the soul and He who proportioned it﴾ ﴿Then He inspired it with its wickedness and its piety﴾ [al-Shams: 7–8], they said: The soul comprises the whole of a human being's creation, with his body, his spirit, and his human faculties, of thought and conduct... and so on.

It has also been said: "The soul" here means the faculties of thought, which perceive the seat of desire and choice. On this view, the mention of the soul in the first sense means that its proportioning is the evenness of its creation and the composition of its organs, which is an utmost indication of power, perfection, and knowledge, as in His saying: ﴿We have certainly created man in the best of stature﴾ [al-Tin: 4], and He said: ﴿And in yourselves; will you not then see?﴾ [al-Dhariyat: 21], meaning: of organs, parts, and compositions, and of many systems that dazzle the intellects: in hearing, in sight, in smell, in taste, and in the senses; and within the body there is what is greater still. Thus it is fitting that He swear by it.

(p-540) "And He who proportioned it": that is, by overwhelming power and comprehensive knowledge. Its mention in the second sense is, in my view, greater than the first sense; this is because the faculties that perceive, think, and determine matters, and that possess choice, among which are acceptance and rejection, contentment and displeasure, taking and withholding, constitute an independent world.

And it is, as we have said, greater than what preceded; for regarding the created aspect, He, exalted is He, said: ﴿The creation of the heavens and the earth is greater than the creation of mankind﴾ [Ghafir: 57]. But in this aspect He said: ﴿Indeed, We offered the trust to the heavens and the earth and the mountains, but they declined to bear it and feared it; and man bore it. Indeed, he was unjust and ignorant﴾ [al-Ahzab: 72].

It is known that some individuals of mankind bore it with truthfulness, discharged it with fidelity, and attained the pleasure of God, exalted is He. May God be pleased with them, and they with Him.

So this soul, in its proportioning for receiving the meanings of good and evil, and for receiving the divine inspiration of wickedness and piety, is a greater indication of power than those inanimate things that neither initiate nor restore, and that possess neither the power to take nor to give.

Here is a simple example of the recently invented devices for storage and calculation, such as the calculator and the electronic "brain." They do not err, as people say, and they have dazzled minds in their description. Yet with a simple glance we find them before the human soul like a drop from a sea.

So we say: First, they are of the making of this soul, which possesses developing perception and remarkable deduction.

Second: they do not err, because they are not capable of erring; error arises from intellectual exertion (ijtihad), and they have no exertion. They merely indicate according to what has been inscribed for them, like material recorded on a tape: the recorder, despite the precision of its retention, cannot add or omit a single letter.

As for man, he changes and substitutes. When he substitutes one word for another, it is either because of his power to produce the other word, or because of his choice to abandon the first.

Likewise here: God, exalted is He, created that soul first, then proportioned it in a state that accepts receiving inspiration in its two counterparts: wickedness and piety, and then it takes one of the two paths. Thus the coming of the oath by it after (p-541) those named things is an indication of the greatness of its essence and the strength of its indication of the power of its Creator, while the others are prepared and receptive to receiving God's inspiration.

* *

**Notice.**

In its coming after the cosmic signs, the sun, the moon, night, day, sky, and earth, there is a call to reflect upon those creatures, drawing from them the indication of the power of their Creator, and the proof of the changing of times, the motion of the celestial spheres, and the origination of the sky by building: that this world necessarily has a Maker, and that what is originated and renewed necessarily has an end and annihilation.

Just as Abraham, peace be upon him, presented to Nimrod examples of reasoning for lordship and divinity: he pointed first to the sun, then to the moon, then moved from them to God, glorified is He.

As for His saying: ﴿Then He inspired it with its wickedness and its piety﴾: if "inspired" (alhama) means "guided it and made it clear to it," then it is like His saying: ﴿And We showed him the two paths﴾ [al-Balad: 10], and His saying: ﴿Indeed, We guided him to the way﴾ [al-Insan: 3]. This is the general guidance, which means indication and clarification.

If it means facilitation and imposition, then there arises the difficulty of divine decree (qadar) against chosen good.

The Shaykh (may God's mercy be upon us and him) has discussed this meaning at full length in dispelling the appearance of contradiction.

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿He has certainly succeeded who purifies it﴾ ﴿And he has failed who corrupts it﴾.

This is the answer to the oath in what preceded. The lam has been dropped from the answer (waw) because of the length of separation between the thing sworn by and the thing sworn about.

The Shaykh (may God's mercy be upon us and him) has already drawn attention to this when discussing His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Indeed, that is true: the disputing of the people of the Fire﴾ [Sad: 64], in Surah Sad, and that they used this verse as evidence for it.

The original is: "Indeed, he has succeeded," and the lam was dropped because of the length of the separation. "Zakkaha" means "purified it." The first thing it is purified of is the filth and defilement of polytheism, as God, exalted is He, said: ﴿The polytheists are only impure﴾ [al-Tawba: 28]. Its purification from it is by faith, then from sins by piety, as in His saying, exalted is He: ﴿So do not attribute purity to yourselves; He knows best who is pious﴾ [al-Najm: 32], then by performing acts of obedience: ﴿He has certainly succeeded who purifies himself, and remembers the name of his Lord and prays﴾ [al-A'la: 14–15].

(p-542) There has been difference over the referent of the pronoun in "zakkaha" and "dassaha," and it returns to their disagreement over: ﴿Then He inspired it with its wickedness and its piety﴾: does it return to God, exalted is He, as in ﴿By the soul and He who proportioned it﴾, or does it return to the servant?

For each view, some texts may be cited as evidence. Among what is cited for the first view is His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Rather, God purifies whom He wills, and they will not be wronged even as much as the thread in a date-pit﴾ [al-Nisa': 49], and His saying: ﴿And if not for the bounty of God upon you and His mercy, not one of you would ever have been purified﴾ [al-Nur: 21]. In a hadith, the Prophet (ﷺ) used to say at this verse: "O God, grant my soul its piety and purify it; You are the best to purify it. You are its Guardian and its Master."

Among what is cited for the second view are:

• His saying: ﴿He has certainly succeeded who purifies himself, and remembers the name of his Lord and prays﴾ [al-A'la: 14–15],

• His saying: ﴿And whoever purifies himself, purifies only for himself; and to God is the final return﴾ [Fatir: 18],

• His saying: ﴿And say, "Would you like to purify yourself? And I would guide you to your Lord, so you would fear Him"﴾ [al-Nazi'at: 18–19],

• His saying: ﴿And what would make you know? Perhaps he would be purified﴾ [Abasa: 3].

All of these, as you see, are open to more than one reading, and the difficulty in them is like the difficulty in what precedes.

What appears—and God knows best—is that reconciling these texts is like reconciling those before them, and that whatever the servant purifies himself with, of faith and deed, in obedience and abstention from sin, is by a bounty from God, as in His saying, exalted is He, explicitly stating this: ﴿And if not for the bounty of God upon you and His mercy, not one of you would ever have been purified﴾ [al-Nur: 21].

Every text in which the pronoun returns, or in which purification is attributed to the servant, is by the bounty of God and His mercy, just as He bestowed upon him guidance and success in faith. It is He who bestows upon him success in righteous action and abstention from sins. This is like your saying: "There is no power and no strength except through God," and His saying: ﴿So do not attribute purity to yourselves﴾ [al-Najm: 32], and His saying: ﴿Have you not seen those who attribute purity to themselves?﴾ [al-Nisa': 49]. It is only in the sense of praise and commendation, as in His saying, exalted is He: ﴿The bedouins say, "We have believed." Say, "You have not believed; but say, 'We have submitted'"﴾ [al-Hujurat: 14]. Indeed, in His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Rather, God purifies whom He wills, and they will not be wronged even as much as the thread in a date-pit﴾ [al-Nisa': 49], there is a combination of the two matters, the divine decree (qadari) and the legislated (shar'i): ﴿Rather, God purifies whom He wills﴾ (p-543) by His bounty, ﴿and they will not be wronged even as much as the thread in a date-pit﴾ by His justice. And God knows best.

Commentary of al-Shinqiti (Adwa' al-Bayan) on surah 91, verse 8:

The author said in (*Daf' Iham al-Idtirab 'an Ayat al-Kitab*):

(p-450) In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful.

Surah al-Shams (The Sun)

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And He inspired it with its wickedness and its righteousness.﴾

This indicates that Allah is the One who places wickedness and righteousness in the soul. But there are verses which indicate that the wickedness and righteousness of the servant are by his own choice and will, such as His saying, exalted is He: ﴿So they preferred blindness over guidance﴾ [Fussilat: 17].

And His saying, exalted is He: ﴿They bought error in exchange for guidance﴾ [al-Baqarah: 16], and the like. This is the issue in which the Qadariyyah (the Determinists who deny divine decree, *al-Qadariyyah*) and the Jabriyyah (the Compulsionists, who deny human agency, *al-Jabriyyah*) went astray.

As for the Qadariyyah, they erred by falling short, when they claimed that the servant creates his own deeds independently, without any effect from Allah's power upon them.

As for the Jabriyyah, they erred by going to excess, when they claimed that the servant has no deed at all, so that he could be held accountable for it.

As for the People of the Sunnah and the Community (*Ahl al-Sunnah wa al-Jama'ah*), they neither went to excess nor fell short. They affirmed for the servant voluntary actions. It is known necessarily to all rational people that involuntary movement (*al-harakah al-ittiʿashiyyah*) is not like voluntary movement. They also affirmed that Allah is the Creator of everything, so He is the Creator of the servant, the Creator of his power and his will, and the effect of the servant's power occurs only by the will of Allah, exalted is He.

So the servant and all his actions are by the will of Allah, exalted is He; yet the servant acts by choice, through the power and the will which Allah created in him, performing a voluntary act for which he is rewarded or punished.

Suppose a Jabri debated a Sunni, and the Jabri said: "My argument before my Lord is that I am not independent in any deed, and that His will and decree must take effect in me in accordance with the eternal knowledge. Therefore I am compelled. How, then, does He punish me for a matter over which I have no power to deviate?" The Sunni would say to him: "Every means of guidance that He gave to the guided, He has given to you. He made for you hearing with which you hear, sight with which you see, and intellect with which you understand. He sent to you a Messenger, and He made for you choice and power. Nothing remains after that except success (*al-tawfiq*), which is His pure dominion. If He grants it, it is bounty; and if He withholds it, it is justice."

As He, exalted is He, indicated by His saying: ﴿Say: "To Allah belongs the conclusive argument. If He had willed, He would have guided you all."﴾ [al-An'am: 149]. Meaning: His dominion over success is a conclusive argument against the creation. Whoever is granted it, it is bounty; and whoever is denied it, it is justice.

When Abu Ishaq al-Isfara'ini (*Abu Ishaq al-Isfara'ini*) debated 'Abd al-Jabbar the Mu'tazili (*'Abd al-Jabbar al-Mu'tazili*), 'Abd al-Jabbar said: "Glory be to Him who is exalted above indecency." His intention was that sins such as theft and adultery occur by the will of the servant, not by the will of Allah, because Allah is too exalted and too majestic to will ugly things, in their claim.

Abu Ishaq said: "A word of truth by which falsehood is intended." Then he said: "Glory be to Him, nothing happens in His dominion except what He wills."

'Abd al-Jabbar said: "Do you think He creates it and then punishes me for it?"

Abu Ishaq said: "Do you think you do it by compulsion from Him? Are you the Lord and He is the servant?"

'Abd al-Jabbar said: "Do you see, if He calls me to guidance but decrees for me destruction, do you think He has done me good or evil?"

Abu Ishaq said: "If that from which He withheld you is your own possession, then He has done you evil. But if it belongs to Him, then if He gives you, it is bounty, and if He withholds from you, it is justice." 'Abd al-Jabbar was confounded, and those present said: "By Allah, there is no answer to this."

A Bedouin came to 'Amr ibn 'Ubayd and said to him: "Pray to Allah that He return to me a donkey of mine that was stolen." He said: "O Allah, its donkey was stolen, and You did not will its theft, so return it to him." The Bedouin said to him: "O man, stop your wicked supplication. If it was stolen and He did not will its theft, then He may will its return, and it will not be returned."

Allah has resolved the difficulty of this issue by His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And you do not will except that Allah wills﴾ [al-Insan: 30 / al-Takwir: 29]. He affirmed for the servant a will, and declared that the servant has no will except by the will of Allah, majestic and exalted. So everything proceeds from His power and His will, majestic and exalted.

And His saying: ﴿Say: "To Allah belongs the conclusive argument. If He had willed, He would have guided you all."﴾

(p-452) As for the view of those who interpreted the noble verse as meaning that ﴿And He inspired it with its wickedness and its righteousness﴾ means that He made clear to it the path of good and the path of evil, there is no difficulty in the verse. It was by this meaning that a group of scholars interpreted it. And knowledge is with Allah, exalted is He.

**Commentary of al-Shinqiti (Adwa' al-Bayan) on Surah 91, verse 11:**

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿Thamud denied in their transgression﴾ ﴿When the most wretched of them was sent forth﴾ ﴿Then the Messenger of Allah said to them: "The she-camel of Allah, and her drinking turn"﴾ ﴿But they denied him and hamstrung her﴾. "Thamud" is the name of the tribe to which the denial is attributed, meaning: they denied the Prophet of Allah, Salih. "The most wretched of them" is the one who hamstrung the she-camel. The sending forth (inbi'ath) is attributed to him alone, among what comes after it: ﴿But they denied him and hamstrung her﴾, so the hamstringing is attributed to them (all).

The Shaykh, may Allah's mercy be upon us and upon him, has previously reconciled this in Surah az-Zukhruf. Its substance is that they were in collusion with him, as in His saying: ﴿So they called their companion, and he took (the sword) and hamstrung her﴾ (Al-Qamar: 29). Thus they were partners with him in her slaughter, as the poet said:

"The one who listens to the slander is a partner of its speaker, and the one who provides the food is a partner of the one who eats it."

In the story of Abu Talha concerning the hunting of the wild donkey, the Prophet (ﷺ) asked them while they were in the state of ihram for the 'umrah: "Did any of you point it out to him?" They said: "No." He said: "Did any of you help him in it?" They said: "No." He said: "Then eat." Its implication is that if they had helped or pointed it out, they would have been partners in its hunting and it would have been forbidden to them, due to His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿Do not kill game while you are in the state of ihram﴾ (Al-Ma'idah: 95). Since they were not partners, it was lawful for them. Had they helped or shared in it, it would have been forbidden to them.

Here, since they were pleased, called to him, and he took (the sword), whether their covenants, their gifts, or otherwise, and he alone hamstrung her, this was done in the name of all, so the punishment was in the name of all. From this is derived the killing of a group for one person, and the punishment of the lookout (ribi'ah, the one who watches for the attackers) alongside the perpetrator. And Allah, may He be exalted, knows best.
